Catalan

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

importunar (first-person singular present importuno, first-person singular preterite importuní, past participle importunat)

  1. to bother, to importune

Portuguese

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ĩ.poʁ.tuˈna(ʁ)/ [ĩ.poh.tuˈna(h)]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ĩ.poʁ.tuˈna(ʁ)/ [ĩ.poh.tuˈna(h)]
    • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /ĩ.poɾ.tuˈna(ɾ)/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /ĩ.poʁ.tuˈna(ʁ)/ [ĩ.poχ.tuˈna(χ)]
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ĩ.poɻ.tuˈna(ɻ)/
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ĩ.puɾ.tuˈnaɾ/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ĩ.puɾ.tuˈnaɾ/
    • (Southern Portugal) IPA(key): /ĩ.puɾ.tuˈna.ɾi/

  • Hyphenation: im‧por‧tu‧nar

Verb

[edit]

importunar (first-person singular present importuno, first-person singular preterite importunei, past participle importunado)

  1. to bother; to harass; to importune
    Synonyms: irritar, incomodar

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From importuno +‎ -ar.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /impoɾtuˈnaɾ/ [ĩm.poɾ.t̪uˈnaɾ]
  • Rhymes: -aɾ
  • Syllabification: im‧por‧tu‧nar

Verb

[edit]

importunar (first-person singular present importuno, first-person singular preterite importuné, past participle importunado)

  1. (transitive) to bother, pester
    Synonyms: molestar, insistir
  2. (transitive) to inconvenience
